summary: Backend + focused UI test of HR multi-shift work-settings (feature A) and presence-check (feature B). Created /app/backend/tests/test_hr_shifts_presence.py with 39 pytest cases — 39/39 PASS in 13s covering: work-settings CRUD (add/edit/delete-main-forbidden), shift assignment via employee and via shift (preserves other memberships), permission gating (Salim 403 on general/shifts/legacy settings), legacy /api/hr/attendance/settings mirrors main shift + shifts[], multi-shift daily sheet emits 2 rows/employee with shift_id + row_key + shift_name, /my has multi_shift=true and today_shifts[2] + next_shift, self check-in/out full 7-step lifecycle (first→open→out→other shift→out→'كل فتراتك'→'بالفعل'), mark with shift_id updates only that shift's record (no dup), DELETE record?shift_id=evening deletes only that record, monthly.shifts_count=2 with due_days≈work_days*2, DELETE shift also $pulls it from employees, presence-check settings validation (checks_per_day=11→400, enriched employees on GET), run-now returns plan+dispatch, send-now with employee+'bad' creates 1/skips 'موظف غير موجود' with sent_at/expires_at + notifications type=presence_check w/ data.check_id, /my pending with remaining_seconds>0, confirm 4 branches (biometric false→403 'هويتك'; no coords→400; out-of-range→403 'خارج نطاق'; in-range+bio→200 confirmed; repeat→400), report shape + employee_name enrichment, internal /run requires X-Internal-Key (401 without, 200 with). UI smoke on /hr-work-settings, /hr-attendance, /hr-presence-checks confirmed all required data-testids present (hr-work-settings-hero, shift-card-*, shift-add-btn, work-general, att-set-self/geofence, att-goto-locations, att-add-holiday, att-settings-save, att-goto-work-settings on /hr-attendance, hr-att-tabs-daily, hr-presence-hero, presence-send-now-btn, presence-tabs-settings).

critical_code_review_comments: hr_shifts.py:170 set_shift_employees iterates the full employees collection and issues one update per doc — for large employee sets this is O(N) round-trips; consider two bulk update_many ($addToSet / $pull) calls scoped by `_id $in oids` and `shift_id: shift_id, _id $nin oids` for efficiency.

hr_shifts.py:169 comment notes 'we handle main-shift by inserting explicitly'; the actual code only adds `main_id` to `cur` when `shift_id == main_id`. Employees implicitly on main who are removed from a non-main shift are unaffected — behaves correctly, but the comment is misleading.

hr_attendance.py:187 uses `$or: [{shift_id: sh.id}, {shift_id: {$exists: false}}]` filter with update_one upsert=true — when there are two legacy rows (one without shift_id, one with) this could match the legacy one and leave the shift_id row untouched; risk is limited to migration-era data.
hr_presence.py:296 GET /my always calls dispatch_due(db) — invoking from an employee endpoint may cause a burst under many concurrent employee polls; consider rate-limiting or moving to loop-only.
